Tight lines! 🎣

all_videos_in_window.description:
Our most recent MFCC group fishing trip to the Canyons with Machaca Charters produced tilefish, a ton of tuna, redfish, a silver eel, and of course this beautiful blue marlin (released). Shout out to Lori Rizzo for taking this video of the marlin, and of a very happy Captain Willy Hatch! ⁠
⁠
Blue marlin migrate to the deep-water canyons south of Cape Cod during the summer and early fall to hunt in the nutrient-rich waters created by the Gulf Stream. Anglers target these apex predators along the steep edges of the canyons as they prey upon squid, mackerel, tuna, mahi and many other species.⁠
⁠

all_videos_in_window.title: Surfcasting False Albacore, Cape Cod
all_videos_in_window.description:
Here's a few tips for anyone who has "albie fever" but doesn't own a boat or kayak...⁠
⁠
1) Inlets and jetties in Nantucket and Vineyard Sound during September is where I've had the best luck over the years.⁠
⁠
2) If you think the albies are leader shy, try holding your rod tip high so your leader is out of the water, and your lure is skipping across the surface.⁠
⁠
3) Long casting lures like the 3/4oz silver Hard Shell Jig from Monomoy Tackle which I'm using in this video can help reach fish.⁠
⁠
4) Wear Korkers or studded boots! I forgot them when I filmed this video and I'm honestly lucky I didn't fall and hurt myself.⁠
⁠
Catching false albacore from shore on Cape Cod is no easy task, but it can be done. Good luck!⁠
⁠
Tight lines 🎣⁠
⁠
Ryan

all_videos_in_window.title: Albie Fishing the Elizabeth Islands off Cape Cod
all_videos_in_window.description:
The Elizabeth Islands are one of my favorite places to chase false albacore. Functioning as a natural barrier, they separate Buzzards Bay from Vineyard Sound. The archipelago offers a fascinating mix of complete isolation, ultra-wealthy privacy, and raw New England history.⁠
⁠
When conditions align, baitfish will congregate along the islands drawing the albies in. During this trip with @flatlinercharters from September of a few years ago, the albies were feeding on bay anchovies and readily attacking the Dart 110S from Monomoy Tackle.⁠
⁠
Reeling for a few seconds, and then pausing to allow the lure to sink through the water column, generated bites for me on this trip. But sometimes the albies want the lure skipping along the surface. I have even heard of anglers from MFCC catching them by …

There's been fish cruising in shallow this August. A few subtle twitches, let it slither through the vegetation, and if you're lucky…hooked up!⁠

all_videos_in_window.description: The September bite continues to build across Long Island, with weakfish showing on both the North and South shores while albies, bonito and Spanish mackerel are pushing through in force. Fluke fishing remains steady, with quality keepers still being caught, and offshore anglers are finding everything from mahi to an impressive 100-pound wahoo. We also check in on bluefish action, freshwater bass and panfish, the latest Dreamboat Challenge standings, and upcoming events, including a big weekend at Patchogue Shores Marina. Plus, we hear from our Island correspondents.

all_videos_in_window.title: September 10th 2026 New England Video Fishing Forecast with Dave AndersonNEF 20260910
all_videos_in_window.description:
I think most would classify the start of the 2026 albie run as “weird”. There have been some epic feeds and wild moments, but in it’s opening 10 days, the bite has lacked consistency and the fish are moving around a ton. Striper action is beginning to show signs of organizing into a full-on fall run with isolated blitz action and great catches, particularly to the north. It was also a very good week for fluke fishing, south of Block Island and there has been some good news on rec-sized bluefin as well.

all_videos_in_window.description: And so begins 10 consecutive months of porgy fishing in New Jersey, as the official opening of scup on 9/1 carries through to June of next year with a 10-inch minimum size and 30 fish bag limit.  Fluke season in New Jersey is quickly coming to an end as well come 9/25, while the black sea bass bag limit goes to 10 fish on 9/23.   We lead the week off discussing the New Jersey Marine Fisheries Council meeting on 9/10 and menhaden reduction hearings starting on 9/15, before jumping into local inshore action on out to the offshore grounds (9:15).  Along with those porgies, weakfish (18:25) seem to have made a big showing this month, adding nicely to the mix of fluke, sheepshead and bluefish; but don't forget about the freshwater action (25:25) throughout the tri-state region. all_videos_in_window.description:
https://www.thefisherman.com/category/dream-boat/
Seven species, 70 leaderboard spots, and one Steiger Craft grand prize—the 2026 Dream Boat Fishing Challenge gets underway May 1st.

Every fishing season has its moments. The first spring blackfish that thumps a jig in chilly April water. A fluke drifting across a sandy edge in July. The unmistakable run of a big bluefish cutting through a late-summer tide. Those moments are what keep anglers coming back to the water year after year. For many fishermen, those experiences are reward enough. But for a dedicated group of anglers across the Northeast, the season carries an added element of competition.

Each year, subscribers to The Fisherman Magazine have the opportunity to take part in one of the region’s most unique and challenging fishing c…

We start with Ryan Piper, Long Island subscriber from Huntington, New York, taking the first place in the bluefish category with an 18.49 lb bluefish weighed in at Cow Harbor Bait & Tackle. Talking about first place, we also want to congratulate Ryan on winning first place in the Surfside Hotel [music] Greatest Bluefish Tournament on Earth this past weekend. What a weekend for Ryan. Next up from Jersey City is Ameer Rajahpaul. He's back with a 3.3 lb sea bass weighed in at Bayonne Bait & Tackle, which takes fifth in the sea bass category and gives Ameer a notch up on the leaderboard. Our final entry of the week comes from New England subscriber Frank One Shell from Storrs, Connecticut landing in first place in the sea bass category with a 3.95 pounder weighed in at Hylers Bait & Tackle. With these three entries this week, it changes the leaderboard. In third place now is Mark Borocki, back on the leaderboard in third with 13 points. Taiboo goes down a point and he's now in second place with 21 points. Back on top is Ameer Rajahpaul with 23 points.

all_videos_in_window.description:
This week’s Long Island fishing forecast comes to you from Bergen Bay Docks, where we take a look at the latest action happening across the region. Inshore bluefin remain red hot off Montauk, weakfish are showing in the South Shore bays, bluefish are active around Jones Inlet, and quality fluke continue to come from the western surf. We also highlight a surprise cobia off Coney Island, black drum from Eatons Neck, big porgies at the Middle Grounds, and Ryan Piper’s impressive 18.49-pound bluefish weighed in at Cow Harbor that unofficially won him the WICC Greatest Bluefish Tournament. Plus, we check in with Canyon Runner, preview the latest Dreamboat Challenge standings and spotlight the September issue.

all_videos_in_window.description:
The news you’ve all been waiting for has finally landed. With the Cape run of false albacore lagging way behind what we typically expect, a rush of albies landed Wednesday morning at a well-known central Rhode Island breakwall and the mayhem has begun! We are also still seeing wild blitz action with striped bass and some bluefish in Boston Harbor. Rec tuna action is still best south of Block. Bonito are widespread and trending larger this year. And Long Island Sound has some gator blues in its western half. This looks like a Labor Day Weekend for the ages, make it count!

We also highlight a surprise cobia off Coney Island, black drum from Eatons Neck, big porgies at the Middle Grounds, and Ryan Piper’s impressive 18.49-pound bluefish weighed in at Cow Harbor that unofficially won him the WICC Greatest Bluefish Tournament. Plus, we check in with Canyon Runner, preview the latest Dreamboat Challenge standings and spotlight the September issue.

raw_posts.title: Sun Sept 13 – Whale Watching
raw_posts.content: This trip was a wet but successful one! Rain was falling as we left the dock and continued throughout most of the trip, a reminder of how fortunate we were this season with most of our trips avoiding heavy downfalls and experiencing sunny, summer weather. Nonetheless, we searched for humpbacks seen on previous trips along the shore, finding our first near Montauk town. This whale was first documented by CRESLI on 09/04 and was seen again on 09/05, a juvenile humpback feeding in under 50 feet of water. With short dive intervals, passengers were treated to frequent sightings of the young whale. We spent some time with this animal before moving on to find another. Along the way, we saw at least one ray (species unknown) leaping from the water and a few shearwaters and about a dozen Wilson’s storm…

raw_posts.title: Mon Sept 7 – Whale Watching
raw_posts.content: It was an absolutely beautiful day to spend the holiday on the water! With sunny skies, excellent visibility, and refreshing breezes, we headed out along the shore following reports of whales near the shore. We found our first whale early, a juvenile humpback off the town of Montauk, in 50 feet of water. The whale was likely feeding at depth completing high fluking dives and long down times. A blow belonging to a second whale was observed in the distance so after spending some time with the first one, we headed out to investigate the second. On our way, one of our volunteers spotted a pod of dolphins to our side, so we changed course to check them out. The dolphins, Tamanend’s bottlenose, were broken up into two large groups, totally 70-90 individuals. After enjoying some time with them, we…

raw_posts.content: With just a little more than a week left to our 2026 season, we headed out along the shore following reports of nearshore cetaceans (whales and dolphins) from the previous day (including some encountered on Friday’s trip). raw_posts.title: Sun Aug 30 – Whale Watching
raw_posts.content: As we always do, we began our trip reminding passengers that we have no idea what we will see as these are wild animals that can move tremendous distances and we are here to observe their natural behaviors (this is not a scripted experience with baited or caged animals); every trip is different. On many occasions this season, that has meant surprises that we could have never anticipated; encounters and observations rarely seen and some more often seen, but always unexpected and amazing. Unfortunately, it also means that sometimes we may find no whales or dolphins at all, and although extremely rare, that was the case aboard Sunday’s adventure. As we sailed through the area where two different humpbacks were encountered just the day prior, it was evident that both whales moved on and no sign of them could be…

all_videos.transcript: Thousands of them washed up on the beaches in Provincetown, so out toward the tip of Cape Cod. And this was on the heels of a meteor landing in Cape Cod Bay. And among the theories people were positing for why all these squid were beaching themselves, my favorite was, is this connected to the meteor? all_videos.transcript: Hey, it's me the striper report guy with your northeast offshore fishing rundown for the week of September 2nd, 2026. Let's start from the south and get into it. Since last week the canyons off Maryland and Virginia have given up good numbers of Mahi and white marlin as well as the occasional yellowfin. A little closer to Ocean City there are Mahi all over the pots and some nice midshore wahoo being trolled up on the backside of the full moon. Moving on up the coast, if it's yellowfin you're after take a poke to Tom's Canyon. There have been a good deal of yellows, big eyes and swords caught that way over the past week. In the shipping lanes off New Jersey and western Long Island there are scant bluefin while the bite toward Coimbra and the Bacardi has rebounded quite a bit. You've also got some yellowfin in the mix since the full moon. Some days they're showing up in force, other days it's a tough pick. Find the porpoises, skipjacks or slicks and chicks and hook some poppers before setting up the jig. South of Block and the Elizabeth Islands there aren't many wreck size fish. It's mostly giants being pulled off the draggers. Meanwhile, east of Cape Cod the wreck bite has been on and off but the commercial guys are getting shots at their giants as well. Further north from Stellwagen to Jeffries you have a few wreck bluefin here and there but the big news this week coming out of New England is the 500 lb state record swordfish caught within 10 mi of the coast of Maine. For the full northeast offshore report visit the OnTheWater YouTube channel every Wednesday at 5:00 p.m. Have a great week guys. Go get them.

all_videos.title: Surfcasting False Albacore, Cape Cod
all_videos.description:
Here's a few tips for anyone who has "albie fever" but doesn't own a boat or kayak...⁠
⁠
1) Inlets and jetties in Nantucket and Vineyard Sound during September is where I've had the best luck over the years.⁠
⁠
2) If you think the albies are leader shy, try holding your rod tip high so your leader is out of the water, and your lure is skipping across the surface.⁠
⁠
3) Long casting lures like the 3/4oz silver Hard Shell Jig from Monomoy Tackle which I'm using in this video can help reach fish.⁠
⁠
4) Wear Korkers or studded boots! I forgot them when I filmed this video and I'm honestly lucky I didn't fall and hurt myself.⁠
⁠
Catching false albacore from shore on Cape Cod is no easy task, but it can be done. Good luck!⁠
⁠
Tight lines 🎣⁠
⁠
Ryan

all_videos.title: Albie Fishing the Elizabeth Islands off Cape Cod
all_videos.description:
The Elizabeth Islands are one of my favorite places to chase false albacore. Functioning as a natural barrier, they separate Buzzards Bay from Vineyard Sound. The archipelago offers a fascinating mix of complete isolation, ultra-wealthy privacy, and raw New England history.⁠
⁠
When conditions align, baitfish will congregate along the islands drawing the albies in. During this trip with @flatlinercharters from September of a few years ago, the albies were feeding on bay anchovies and readily attacking the Dart 110S from Monomoy Tackle.⁠
⁠
Reeling for a few seconds, and then pausing to allow the lure to sink through the water column, generated bites for me on this trip. But sometimes the albies want the lure skipping along the surface. I have even heard of anglers from MFCC catching them by …

all_videos.title: Fishing Weed Beds Without Getting Hung Up
all_videos.description:
There's been fish cruising in shallow this August. A few subtle twitches, let it slither through the vegetation, and if you're lucky…hooked up!⁠

The single hook on soft plastics like the Super Snax means you can work right through the weeds without getting hung up. It also makes releasing fish a lot easier.⁠
⁠
Really been loving this style of fishing on my lighter 8'6" rod — makes fighting fish way more fun.⁠
⁠
Tight lines! 🎣⁠

all_videos.description:
I think most would classify the start of the 2026 albie run as “weird”. There have been some epic feeds and wild moments, but in it’s opening 10 days, the bite has lacked consistency and the fish are moving around a ton. Striper action is beginning to show signs of organizing into a full-on fall run with isolated blitz action and great catches, particularly to the north. It was also a very good week for fluke fishing, south of Block Island and there has been some good news on rec-sized bluefin as well.

all_videos.title: The Fisherman 2026 Dream Boat Challenge Update September 2nd, 2026
all_videos.description:
https://www.thefisherman.com/category/dream-boat/
Seven species, 70 leaderboard spots, and one Steiger Craft grand prize—the 2026 Dream Boat Fishing Challenge gets underway May 1st.

Every fishing season has its moments. The first spring blackfish that thumps a jig in chilly April water. A fluke drifting across a sandy edge in July. The unmistakable run of a big bluefish cutting through a late-summer tide. Those moments are what keep anglers coming back to the water year after year. For many fishermen, those experiences are reward enough. But for a dedicated group of anglers across the Northeast, the season carries an added element of competition.

Each year, subscribers to The Fisherman Magazine have the opportunity to take part in one of the region’s most unique and challenging fishing c…
all_videos.transcript: It's the first week of September and it's time for the Dream Boat Challenge update. We start with Ryan Piper, Long Island subscriber from Huntington, New York, taking the first place in the bluefish category with an 18.49 lb bluefish weighed in at Cow Harbor Bait & Tackle. Talking about first place, we also want to congratulate Ryan on winning first place in the Surfside Hotel [music] Greatest Bluefish Tournament on Earth this past weekend. What a weekend for Ryan. Next up from Jersey City is Ameer Rajahpaul. He's back with a 3.3 lb sea bass weighed in at Bayonne Bait & Tackle, which takes fifth in the sea bass category and gives Ameer a notch up on the leaderboard. Our final entry of the week comes from New England subscriber Frank One Shell from Storrs, Connecticut landing in first place in the sea bass category with a 3.95 pounder weighed in at Hylers Bait & Tackle. With these three entries this week, it changes the leaderboard. In third place now is Mark Borocki, back on the leaderboard in third with 13 points. Taiboo goes down a point and he's now in second place with 21 points. Back on top is Ameer Rajahpaul with 23 points.

all_videos.description:
This week’s Long Island fishing forecast comes to you from Bergen Bay Docks, where we take a look at the latest action happening across the region. Inshore bluefin remain red hot off Montauk, weakfish are showing in the South Shore bays, bluefish are active around Jones Inlet, and quality fluke continue to come from the western surf. We also highlight a surprise cobia off Coney Island, black drum from Eatons Neck, big porgies at the Middle Grounds, and Ryan Piper’s impressive 18.49-pound bluefish weighed in at Cow Harbor that unofficially won him the WICC Greatest Bluefish Tournament. Plus, we check in with Canyon Runner, preview the latest Dreamboat Challenge standings and spotlight the September issue.

all_videos.title: September 3rd 2026 New England Video Fishing Forecast with Dave Anderson
all_videos.description:
The news you’ve all been waiting for has finally landed. With the Cape run of false albacore lagging way behind what we typically expect, a rush of albies landed Wednesday morning at a well-known central Rhode Island breakwall and the mayhem has begun! We are also still seeing wild blitz action with striped bass and some bluefish in Boston Harbor. Rec tuna action is still best south of Block. Bonito are widespread and trending larger this year. And Long Island Sound has some gator blues in its western half. This looks like a Labor Day Weekend for the ages, make it count!

all_videos.title: September 3rd 2026 Long Island Metro Fishing Report with Matthew Broderick
all_videos.description:
This week’s Long Island fishing forecast comes to you from Bergen Bay Docks, where we take a look at the latest action happening across the region. Inshore bluefin remain red hot off Montauk, weakfish are showing in the South Shore bays, bluefish are active around Jones Inlet, and quality fluke continue to come from the western surf. We also highlight a surprise cobia off Coney Island, black drum from Eatons Neck, big porgies at the Middle Grounds, and Ryan Piper’s impressive 18.49-pound bluefish weighed in at Cow Harbor that unofficially won him the WICC Greatest Bluefish Tournament. Plus, we check in with Canyon Runner, preview the latest Dreamboat Challenge standings and spotlight the September issue.
